product: B2B online-casino supplier and live-casino market leader: Crazy Time, Lightning Roulette, Monopoly Live and other game shows, live tables, and RNG slots via NetEnt, Red Tiger, Big Time Gaming, Nolimit City, Ezugi and DigiWheel. Recent launches include Disco Balls (9 Sep 2026) and Monopoly Roulette/Roll'em.
demand: Demand tracks market regulation and opening: Latin America +26.3% y/y, North America +9.5% y/y with Alberta regulated in July 2026 and Monopoly Live live in four states, Europe +3.5% q/q, Africa/other +14.2% q/q, while Asia fell 3.7% q/q on cybercrime. Ice Fishing remains a top recent launch.
pricing_power: Mixed. Live-casino leadership and exclusivity wins such as Boyd imply real negotiating power over operators, but group revenue fell 1.2% y/y, the CEO cites low European channelization, and no price increases are disclosed; the 65.9% EBITDA margin was held by cost control rather than pricing.
competition: Live casino: Playtech, Pragmatic Play, Stakelogic, Light & Wonder and operator in-house studios. Slots: Pragmatic Play, Light & Wonder, Hacksaw and Relax Gaming. Evolution is the live-casino leader but competition intensifies as US states and Latin America open, and channelization stays a live risk in Europe.
team: CEO Martin Carlesund, CFO Joakim Andersson, CCO Marcus Huber; founder-led heritage with co-founder Fredrik Osterberg now a board director, marking Evolution's 20th anniversary in 2026. The board recommends rejecting the Candle Lake SEK 695 offer; governance attention centers on major shareholder Kenneth Dart's roughly 30% stake.
market_strategy: Vertically integrated B2B: build games, studios and platform in-house, expand state-by-state in the US and in Latin America (Argentina studio relaunch, Brazil Ice Fishing) alongside Europe, grow RNG and game shows, and return cash via buybacks and dividends while rejecting the Candle Lake offer.
bull: Q2 2026 revenue -1.2% y/y but constant-currency +2.4%; Latin America +26.3%, North America +9.5%, Europe +3.5% q/q; EBITDA margin held 65.9%; Boyd exclusivity won 18 Sep 2026; buybacks ongoing.
bear: Revenue still shrinking y/y (1H -1.4%); Asia -3.7% q/q on cybercrime; GBP 4.75m UKGC settlement; ~30% Candle Lake/Dart overhang with rejected SEK 695 bid; JPMorgan Underweight SEK 660 and Goldman Sell SEK 610 both below 833 SEK.
falsifier: Q3 2026 report on 23 Oct 2026 shows group revenue still negative y/y and EBITDA margin below 65%, proving the recovery thesis wrong.
sources: analyst actions and share price read via MarketScreener (aggregator) feed; Yahoo Finance, Reuters, WSJ, investing.com, stockanalysis and tipranks were attempted but blocked or paywalled
web_what_changed: Q2 2026 (17 Jul 2026): net revenue EUR 517.8m, -1.2% y/y, EBITDA margin 65.9%. Candle Lake reached 30.02% of votes on 24 Jul 2026 and on 13 Aug 2026 launched a mandatory cash offer at SEK 695 per share; Evolution board recommends shareholders do NOT accept. GBP 4.75m UK Gambling Commission settlement; Galaxy Gaming deal lapsed 17 Jul 2026; buybacks and an EGM on 22 Sep 2026.
web_not_known_yesterday: On 25 Sep 2026 Evolution published its Nomination Committee for the 2027 AGM, and major shareholder Kenneth Dart declined a committee seat. Same day JPMorgan raised its target to SEK 660 (from 565), reiterating Underweight. 24 Sep 2026: founder Fredrik Osterberg 20th-anniversary article. Share price 833.00 SEK on 25 Sep 2026.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Volume and mix, not price: Q2 2026 revenue fell 1.2% y/y (constant-currency +2.4%). Latin America +26.3% y/y, North America +9.5% y/y, Europe +3.5% q/q after several down quarters, Asia -3.7% q/q, Africa/other +14.2% q/q. RNG rose to EUR 80.5m. Game shows and native-language tables drove mix; no price lever disclosed.
web_suppliers: Largely vertically integrated: games, studios and platform are built in-house, so no single-source content supplier. Key inputs are studio real estate, about 22,900 staff, camera/streaming hardware and gaming licences (Malta, UK and others). No supplier constraint is disclosed; hiring, studio capacity and regulatory approvals are the real constraints.
web_customers: B2B: 870 operators at Q2 2026. Named relationship: Boyd Interactive (Stardust, Resorts, Mohegan Sun) became exclusive Evolution live-dealer brands on 18 Sep 2026. Evolution does not disclose customer-level concentration, though a few tier-one operators likely dominate. 2025 sales billed via Malta 82.2% and Curacao 10.4%.
web_who_loses: Rival live-casino and slots suppliers: Playtech, Pragmatic Play, Light & Wonder, Stakelogic, plus operator in-house studios. Boyd exclusivity displaces competing live-dealer providers at Stardust, Resorts and Mohegan Sun. Smaller studios and land-based casinos lose share as regulated live online grows.
web_contradicting_evidence: Revenue is still shrinking y/y (Q2 2026 -1.2%, 1H -1.4%); Asia is volatile and hit by cybercrime; the CEO flags low European channelization. A GBP 4.75m UKGC settlement and an unresolved ~30% Candle Lake/Dart overhang whose SEK 695 bid the board rejects. JPMorgan Underweight target SEK 660 and Goldman Sell SEK 610 both sit below the 833 SEK price.
web_if_management_right: Europe keeps its q/q recovery, Latin America compounds above 20%, North America stays high-single-digit on state openings and new studios (Alberta, second Michigan studio), RNG and game shows scale, buybacks shrink the share count, and the 65-66% EBITDA margin holds; growth re-accelerates into the Q3 2026 report on 23 Oct 2026.
web_if_management_wrong: Asia volatility and cybercrime persist, European channelization stalls, revenue stays negative and the 65%+ margin erodes on studio, staffing and compliance costs. With the 833 SEK price above every bear target and a rejected SEK 695 Candle Lake bid, the stock has little valuation cushion if growth does not return.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Operators carrying Evolution content (Boyd Interactive, Stardust, Resorts, Mohegan Sun, plus large global operators) gain premium live entertainment; live-streaming, camera and studio-infrastructure vendors; licensing jurisdictions such as Malta; Hasbro via the Monopoly licensing deal; shareholders through ongoing buybacks.
